newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan stocks in upward trend at end of weekly trade.
newsitem.headline: Jordan stocks in upward trend at end of weekly trade.

text.p: Jordanian stocks kept up four month highs at end of weekly trade on Wednesday with heavy select demand on high performing companies, brokers said.
The official Amman Financial Market 60-share index climbed 0.72 percent to 148.42 points, its highest level since May, in a strong turnover of 396,144 shares worth 1.66 million dinars ($2.3 million).
"There was good selective buying on stock that have posted healthy half-year results," said Assad al-Dissi, general manager of Amman Financial and Securities Company.
Dissi said both medium sized portfolios and some foreign buying along with floor trader activity helped underpin the market's revived trade.
The market fell at end of June to levels unreached since 1993 on a cash shortage and minimal institutional support.

Arab Bank -- with nearly 60 percent of total volume -- was once again was the market leader, pulling other stock in its path and gaining 3.50 dinars to 244.00 after shares worth 999,800 dinars changed hands.
Livestock and Poultry kept up heavy demand that has persisted for over two weeks with another 20 fils rise to 710 fils after shares worth 89,522 dinars were traded.
The Pearl Investable Index -- an independent index of the 45 best-performing shares from the official market -- rose 0.61 percent to 82.03 points, still 14.11 percent down on last year.
